cls: Inactivated bacterial toxoid (active immunization against tetanus)
quick: 0.5 mL IM into deltoid muscle; primary series 3 doses (0, 1-2, 6-12 mo); booster every 10 years (or 5 years for dirty/tetanus-prone wounds)
Intramuscular into deltoid muscle; shake well before use
Recommended and safe; standard maternal immunization (2 doses of Td/TT in pregnancy or 1 dose Tdap at 27-36 weeks) prevents neonatal tetanus
Clean minor wound: vaccine if >=10 yr since last dose; all other/dirty wounds: vaccine if >=5 yr + TIG (250-500 IU) if unimmunized/unknown
Local injection site pain, swelling; observe 15 min for allergic reactions
summary: Tetanus toxoid (available as adsorbed TT, adult Td, or Tdap containing acellular pertussis) provides active immunity against tetanus caused by the neurotoxin tetanospasmin of Clostridium tetani. It is indicated for primary immunization, decennial routine adult boosters, wound-management prophylaxis following trauma or animal bites, and maternal immunization during pregnancy to eliminate maternal and neonatal tetanus. It is given intramuscularly (0.5 mL) into the deltoid muscle.
indications: Primary active immunization against tetanus in infants, children, and adults
Routine decennial booster immunization in adults (preferably Td or Tdap every 10 years)
Post-exposure tetanus prophylaxis in wound management following burns, trauma, compound fractures, puncture wounds, or animal/human bites
Maternal immunization during pregnancy to prevent maternal and neonatal tetanus mortality

dosage.n: Prefer Td (tetanus-reduced diphtheria) or Tdap to maintain diphtheria and pertussis herd immunity.

dosage.d: 0.5 mL IM if >=10 years since last dose (or if <3 primary doses/unknown)
dosage.n: Tetanus Immune Globulin (TIG) NOT needed for clean minor wounds regardless of vaccination history.

dosage.c: Wound management - dirty / contaminated / tetanus-prone wound
dosage.d: 0.5 mL IM if >=5 years since last dose. If <3 primary doses or unknown: 0.5 mL IM vaccine PLUS TIG 250-500 IU IM at separate anatomical site
dosage.n: Tetanus-prone: wounds contaminated with dirt, feces, soil, saliva; puncture wounds; avulsions; crush injuries; frostbite; burns.

dosage.d: Td/TT: 2 doses 4 weeks apart (first early in 2nd trimester, second at least 4 weeks later and >=2 weeks before delivery); or Tdap single dose at 27-36 weeks
dosage.t: 2 doses (or 1 Tdap booster if previously vaccinated)
dosage.n: Protects mother and transfers protective IgG transplacentally to prevent neonatal tetanus.

dosage.d: 0.5 mL IM at 0, 4-8 weeks, and 6-12 months
dosage.n: Substitute Tdap for one of the doses to provide pertussis protection.

admin: Inject strictly intramuscularly into the deltoid muscle (adults/older children) or anterolateral thigh (infants). Avoid subcutaneous injection (causes sterile abscesses or granulomas due to aluminum adjuvant).
Shake vial or prefilled syringe thoroughly before drawing to resuspend the adsorbed toxoid into a uniform cloudy suspension.
When Tetanus Immune Globulin (TIG) is required concurrently, administer TIG and vaccine at separate anatomical sites using separate syringes.
Do not freeze; store between 2°C and 8°C.
moa: Inactivated Clostridium tetani exotoxin (formalin-detoxified tetanospasmin adsorbed onto aluminum salts) stimulates the production of specific neutralizing antitoxin IgG antibodies. Circulating antitoxin binds and neutralizes free tetanospasmin before it can bind irreversibly to gangliosides on presynaptic inhibitory interneurons (Renshaw cells) in the spinal cord, preventing spastic paralysis.

absolute: Severe acute anaphylaxis or encephalopathy within 7 days following a previous dose of tetanus toxoid-containing vaccine
relative: Severe Arthus-type hypersensitivity reaction following a prior tetanus toxoid dose (defer booster for >=10 years even for tetanus-prone wounds)
Guillain-Barré syndrome within 6 weeks following a previous tetanus toxoid dose
Moderate to severe acute febrile illness (defer routine non-urgent vaccination)
monitor: Local injection site soreness, induration, erythema
Mild transient fever, headache, body aches

preg: Safe & strongly recommended. Maternal immunization with Td or Tdap is standard of care worldwide to prevent neonatal and puerperal tetanus.
common_se: Injection site pain, erythema, swelling, warmth (50-80%)
serious_se: Arthus-type type III hypersensitivity (extensive limb swelling in individuals with excessively high pre-existing antitoxin titers)
Severe anaphylaxis (extremely rare, ~1-2 per million doses)
monitoring: Ensure documentation of vaccination in patient's health record / immunization passport
Observe patient for 15 minutes post-injection for acute hypersensitivity reactions
